I am a researcher interested in the causes and consequences of animal movement, and the emerging technologies that we can use to track animals in the wild. I am especially concerned with changes in animal movement behaviour caused by climate change.

I'm currently a Research Fellow at the [Centre for Biodiversity and Conservation Science](https://cbcs.centre.uq.edu.au/profile/3189/lily-bentley), based at the University of Queensland. I work with Associate Professor Daniel Dunn in the [Applied Marine Biogeography Lab](https://www.marinebiogeo.org/the-lab) on projects related to migratory connectivity in the ocean.

Together with WWF and a group of international partners, I work on [Blue Corridors for Turtles](https://www.argos-system.org/new-global-initiative-map-blue-corridors-for-turtles/). The [first report](https://wwfafrica.awsassets.panda.org/downloads/blue-corridors-for-turtles_report.pdf) from the project was launched at the UN Ocean Conference in June 2025.

Closer to home, I'm tracking seabirds in the Great Barrier Reef in partnership with BirdLife Australia and Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service, to find out which areas matter most for their conservation.

In 2022 I completed my PhD as a [Gates Cambridge](https://www.gatescambridge.org) scholar, in partnership with the [Department of Zoology](https://www.zoo.cam.ac.uk) and the [British Antarctic Survey](https://www.bas.ac.uk), on albatross and petrel foraging ecology.

I spent most of 2017 undertaking a Data Science fellowship in the Kampala office of Fenix International, a solar power company bringing affordable clean energy to off-grid customers in Uganda.

My previous research was in the Franklin ECO-Lab at the University of Queensland, where I investigated saltwater crocodile thermal biology and movement ecology.

Outside of academia, I worked for eight years in Animal Training & Behaviour at the [RSPCA Queensland](https://www.rspcaqld.org.au), teaching obedience, agility, puppy classes, and individual training.

Find out more about my [Research](research.qmd), [Teaching](teaching.qmd) and [Outreach](outreach.qmd), or see my publications on [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ZLBy3hIAAAAJ&hl=en).
